title: Instruction following mega-issue in Claude Code / Cursor
text:
Have noticed a handful of issues w/ instruction-following off of the base CLAUDE.md / main-kurt.mdc cursor rule file: 

1. Failing to identify when the user is attempting to add a new format template
2. Failing to update the `plan.md` with progress within a project 
3. Making a single attempt at source gathering (via external research or internal content list) and moving on if nothing found (rather than fanning out to other query variants).  
4. Source gathering output is not clearly defined, so the agent freelances (creates random `/project/research/` files, rather than writing to `plan.md` or a `project/sources.md` with citations.  
5. Agent is confused about separation of document metadata (in db) + actual source docs in filesystem.  Need to explicitly require search / list / get via kurt rather than grep.

title: 🚀 Разработка репозитория интеграции Claude Code с AWS Bedrock для Cursor (полная автоматизация через Cursor Agent)
text:
## 🎯 Цель проекта

Создать production-ready репозиторий для интеграции Claude Code с AWS Bedrock, обеспечивающий доступ к Claude моделям (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5) через AWS инфраструктуру для использования в Cursor IDE.

**КРИТИЧЕСКИ ВАЖНО**: Вся реализация проекта должна выполняться автоматически через **Cursor Agent в Linear**.

---

## 🤖 Автоматизация через Cursor Agent

### Workflow:

1. Задача создается в Linear → синхронизируется с GitHub issue
2. Cursor Agent получает контекст задачи из Linear (через GraphQL API)
3. Cursor Agent автоматически генерирует код согласно требованиям
4. Код коммитится в GitHub с автоматическими PR
5. Linear task обновляется с прогрессом в real-time
6. CI/CD pipeline запускается автоматически
7. Результаты возвращаются в Linear для tracking

### Требования к Cursor Agent:

* ✅ Доступ к Linear GraphQL API
* ✅ Автоматическое чтение контекста задач
* ✅ Генерация кода для всех 8 фаз
* ✅ Обновление прогресса в Linear
* ✅ Синхронизация с GitHub Actions

---

## 📋 Основные компоненты по DEPLOYMENT документации

### Фаза 1: AWS Infrastructure Setup 🔧

- [ ] Настройка AWS аккаунта с Bedrock
- [ ] Конфигурация IAM (bedrock:InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream, ListInferenceProfiles)
- [ ] **Terraform IaC** для всех AWS ресурсов (создается Cursor Agent)
- [ ] AWS CLI automation
- [ ] Bedrock Console use case form

### Фаза 2: Claude Code Configuration ⚙️

- [ ] Скрипты для всех переменных окружения:

  - `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=1024`
- [ ] Скрипты валидации конфигурации

### Фаза 3: Authentication Methods 🔐

title: [FEATURE] Video Input Support in Claude Code
text:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing requests](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Aenhancement) and this feature hasn't been requested yet
- [x] This is a single feature request (not multiple features)

### Problem Statement

**Summary**

Add the ability to paste or reference video files in Claude Code CLI, similar to the existing image/screenshot support.
Motivation
Claude Code currently supports pasting screenshots and referencing image files, which is extremely useful for UI debugging and visual context. However, there's no support for video input, which limits the tool's usefulness in scenarios like:

UI/UX debugging: Demonstrating animation bugs, transition issues, or interaction problems that can't be captured in a single frame
Screen recordings: Sharing quick recordings of bug reproduction steps
Mobile app development: Showing gesture-based interactions or scroll behaviors
Code walkthroughs: Providing video context of terminal output or build processes

Supported formats (suggested)

MP4
WebM
MOV
GIF (animated)

Implementation considerations

Video files can be large; consider adding a size limit or automatic compression
Option to extract key frames automatically if full video processing isn't feasible
Could leverage Claude's vision capabilities on extracted frames as an intermediate solution

Environment:

Platform: All (macOS, Linux, Windows)
Feature type: Enhancement

### Proposed Solution

Add video input support to Claude Code with the following capabilities:

Paste video from clipboard (similar to current image paste with Ctrl+V)
Drag and drop video files into the terminal
Reference video file paths directly in prompts (e.g., @video.mp4)

### Alternative Solutions

Manual frame extraction: Users can extract screenshots from videos manually, but this is cumbersome and loses temporal context
Text descriptions: Describing video content in text is imprecise and time-consuming

### Priority

High - Sign

title: [FEATURE] Add support for Claude Code
text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently, Strix requires LLM API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic API, etc.) which adds operational overhead - managing API keys, tracking usage/costs, and dealing with rate limits. I'm always frustrated when I need to expose API keys in CI/CD environments or when running security assessments on air-gapped systems. Additionally, for developers already using Claude Code for agentic development, it would be more convenient to use a single tool instead of managing separate API integrations.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add support for Claude Code as an LLM provider option. Claude Code is Anthropic's command-line tool for agentic coding that provides a more integrated developer experience without requiring direct API key management.

Configuration example:
```bash
# Instead of
export STRIX_LLM="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
export LLM_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."

# Use
export STRIX_LLM="claude-code/claude-sonnet-4.5"
strix --target ./app-directory
```

This would allow Strix to leverage Claude Code's existing authentication and session management, providing:
- No need to expose API keys in environment variables
- Better integration with existing Claude Code workflows
- Simplified setup for developers already using Claude Code
- Potential for better token usage optimization through Claude Code's session management

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

1. **Local LLM via LMStudio/Ollama** - Works but requires significant local resources and doesn't match the quality of Claude models
2. **API proxy service** - Building a middleware service to abstract API key management, but this adds unnecessary complexity
3. **Environment-specific key rotation** - Using secrets management tools (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), but still requires API key exposure at runtime
4. **Wrapper scripts** - Creating shell scripts that inject API keys, but this is a workaround rather than a proper solution

# Installation Guide: document-edit-mcp for Claude Code in Cursor IDE

## Overview

This guide documents the installation process, issues encountered, and working solutions for installing the `document-edit-mcp` server in **Claude Code for VS Code** running through **Cursor IDE** on Windows.

1. [Problems Encountered](#problems-encountered)

7. [System Requirements](#system-requirements)

---

## Problems Encountered

### Issue 1: Module Import Error
**Error Message:**
```
Error: No module named 'document_edit_mcp'
```

**Context:**
- Initial installation via `claude mcp add` completed successfully
- MCP server appeared in the MCP list but showed as disconnected
- Health check failed with module import error
- The server was unable to start despite Python dependencies being installed

### Issue 2: Package Naming Inconsistency
**Problem:**
- Repository name: `document-edit-mcp` (with hyphens - this is fine)
- Internal Python module folder: Must use underscores, not hyphens
- Python module name expected: `document_edit_mcp` (with underscores)
- Server command in config: `python -m document_edit_mcp.server`

**The Core Issue:**
Python cannot import modules with hyphens in their names. While package names on PyPI can use hyphens, the actual Python module directory inside the package must use underscores. The original package may not have properly structured its internal folders to use underscores, causing the import failure.

### Issue 3: Virtual Environment Path Issues
**Problem:**
- Windows path handling with spaces and special characters
- Virtual environment activation in MCP context
- Python executable not found in expected locations

---

title: ENH: Feature request / Idea: Custom CodeAgent: Codex, Claude Code, OpenHeands, Copilot etc
text:
<!--
Thank you for suggesting an idea to improve this project!
Please provide as much detail as possible.
-->

**Problem**
Instead of competing with SotA Coding Agents that focus on code generation, Smolagents could benefit from integrating with them.

While Smolagents is excellent in creating a general agentic framework, enforcing the security limitations of the produced code, retry mechanisms, and code output verification, it can leverage SotA Coding Agents' superior capabilities in producing high-quality code and testing it.

The Code Agent should be able to use state-of-the-art external coding agents on tests like those listed in the well-established and respected [SWE-Bench Verified](https://www.swebench.com/) benchmarking. 

**Proposed solution**
Provide a CustomCodeAgent that could integrate with OpenHands, Codex, Claude Code, Copilot, [SWE-agent](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent), [TRAE-Agent](https://github.com/bytedance/trae-agent), [Refact](https://github.com/smallcloudai/refact), etc.

**Is this not possible with the current options.**
Currently, CodeAgnet is only a SmolAgent implementation.

**Alternatives considered**
Run with 3rd party Code Agent and then provide the results as a context or create a custom LLM wrapper. Which is suboptimal.

**Additional context (optional)**
The listed Coding agents may work locally as CLI, may be imported as a module, or consumed remotely via API.

### Problem Statement

Currently, Claude Code and the Claude web/desktop app operate as completely siloed experiences. If a user has an active Claude subscription and uses both products, there's no continuity between them.

This creates friction in real workflows:
- You might have a deep architectural discussion in Claude.ai, mapping out system design, discussing tradeoffs, iterating on approaches — but when you open Claude Code to actually implement it, you're starting from zero. The context is gone.
- You can't reference previous conversations ("remember that auth flow we discussed?") because Claude Code has no awareness that those conversations exist.
- Users end up copy-pasting summaries from Claude.ai into Claude Code, or re-explaining context that already exists in their chat history.

The two products feel disconnected despite being part of the same ecosystem and often used by the same authenticated user.

### Proposed Solution

Allow Claude Code to optionally access a user's Claude app chat history when authenticated with the same account.

Implementation ideas:
- **Read-only access to conversation history**: Claude Code could query past conversations from Claude.ai to retrieve relevant context when the user references them
- **Explicit user invocation**: Something like `/recall "auth discussion from last week"` or `/context import` to pull in relevant threads
- **Semantic search over history**: Rather than exact matching, allow Claude Code to find conversations by topic/intent
- **Privacy-first**: This should be opt-in, with clear user control over what's accessible

The key is enabling continuity across the product ecosystem for users who want it, without forcing it on those who prefer separation.

title: claude code 529
How to use Claude Code
text: I've been using Claude Code daily for months. Here are my notes ## Extended Thinking: The Magic Words Claude Code has built-in thinking modes that allocate more compute for complex problems: - **"think"** → ~4K tokens - **"think hard"** / **"megathink"** → ~10K tokens - **"think harder"** / **"ultrathink"** → ~32K tokens Example: `ultrathink Plan the architecture for this payment system` Reserve ultrathink for architecture decisions and hard debugging. For simple tasks, you're just burning tokens. --- ## Essential Keyboard Shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | |----------|--------| | `Escape` | Stop current operation | | `Escape` x2 | Searchable message history / rewind to checkpoint | | `Up Arrow` | Command history (persists across sessions) | | `Tab` | Autocomplete file paths | | `Ctrl+V` | Paste images (not Cmd+V, even on Mac) | | `Ctrl+R` | Search prompt history | | `Shift+Tab` | Toggle Plan Mode | | `@filename` | Reference files in prompts | --- ## Plan Mode Toggle with `Shift+Tab`. Claude analyzes your codebase read-only before proposing changes. Use it for: - Exploring unfamiliar codebases - Planning complex refactors - Safe code reviews --- ## CLAUDE.md: Project Memory Create a `CLAUDE.md` in your repo root: ```markdown # Build - npm run build - npm run test # Style - ES modules, not CommonJS - No `any` types - Destructure imports # Workflow - Typecheck after changes - Run single tests, not full suite ``` Keep it concise. Claude loads this automatically every session. **Tip:** Press `#` during a session to give Claude an instruction it will automatically add to the relevant `CLAUDE.md`. --- ## Context Management Tips - **`/clear` often** — Start fresh for new tasks. Old history eats tokens. - **`/compact`** — Summarize context when running low. - **`--resume`** — Continue previous sessions: `claude --resume` -

[FEATURE] Documentation/support for Claude Code
text:
## Feature Description
Documentation and/or tooling to help users register the MCP server with Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI tool), which uses a separate configuration system from Claude Desktop.

  ## Use Case & Motivation
Claude Code is becoming widely used for development workflows. Users who work with Obsidian vaults as knowledge bases benefit greatly from the search tools (semantic search, Dataview queries), even when they have direct filesystem access through Claude Code.

Currently, the plugin registers smoothly with Claude Desktop, but Claude Code uses a completely separate MCP configuration system (on Windows: `~/.claude.json` rather than `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`). Users have to figure out the setup process through trial and error.

  ## Proposed Solution
The simplest solution is to add a "Claude Code Setup" section to the README. Obviously, if this could be automated that's even better. To get this started, I believe these are the steps I went through (with Claude Code's help) to get the server registered to my Claude code:

**1. Add the server via CLI**
`claude mcp add --transport stdio obsidian-mcp-tools --scope user -- "C:\path\to\mcp-server.exe"`

This creates an entry in ~/.claude.json (on Windows: C:\Users\<username>\.claude.json)

**2. Manually add environment variables**
The CLI command creates the server entry but with an empty env: {} object. Manually edit ~/.claude.json to
add the API key:
```
  "mcpServers": {
    "obsidian-mcp-tools": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\mcp-server.exe",
      "args": [],
      "env": {
        "OBSIDIAN_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here"
      }
    }
  }
```

User: "Help me workshop my classification prompt"

Claude Code CLI has an `/ide` command that connects to IDEs like VSCode and Cursor, enabling:
- Real-time file change tracking
- Automatic diff display when files are modified
- Seamless navigation between terminal and editor

Currently, running `/ide` in Claude Code inside Wave Terminal shows no connection because Wave Terminal isn't recognized as a supported IDE.

**As a user, I would like Wave Terminal to support Claude Code's `/ide` integration**, so that:
1. `/ide` command recognizes and connects to Wave Terminal
2. File modifications from Claude Code are reflected in Wave's editor/preview widgets
3. Users get the same AI-assisted coding experience as in VSCode/Cursor

This would likely require:
- Implementing the protocol/API that Claude Code uses to communicate with IDEs
- Exposing Wave Terminal's editor and file preview widgets to external tools
- May need coordination with Anthropic's Claude Code team on their IDE integration spec

text:
## Summary

Add support for multi-agent workflows that combine Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and OpenAI Codex CLI to enable more powerful and flexible automation scenarios.

## Background / Investigation Results

We conducted an investigation to determine the feasibility of integrating multiple AI agent CLIs within cc-wf-studio workflows.

### CLI Availability Confirmed

| CLI | Version | Command |
|-----|---------|---------|
| Claude Code | 2.1.23 | `claude` |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | 0.0.398 | `copilot` |
| OpenAI Codex CLI | 0.92.0 | `codex` |

### Key Finding: Full stdout Access from Parent Agent

When Claude Code invokes child agents (Copilot/Codex) via Bash, **all stdout is captured and accessible** in the `tool_result`:

```json
{
  "type": "tool_result",
  "content": "OpenAI Codex v0.92.0...\nthinking\n**Preparing response**\n..."
}
```

Using `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, the workflow engine can access complete execution data.

### Output Detail Comparison

| Information | Copilot CLI | Codex CLI |
|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| Final output | ✅ | ✅ |
| Thinking process | ❌ Not exposed | ✅ `thinking` section |
| MCP status | ❌ | ✅ `mcp: ready` |
| Model info | ✅ `claude-sonnet-4.5` | ✅ `gpt-5.2-codex` |
| Token usage | ✅ `37.3k in, 268 out` | ✅ `5,609` |
| API time | ✅ `7s` | ❌ |

### Architecture Feasibility

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Workflow Engine (cc-wf-studio)                         │
│  --output-format stream-json for full data access       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                          ↓                              │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐     │
│  │ Claude Code │  │ Copilot CLI │  │ Codex CLI   │     │
│  │ stdout: ✅  │  │ stdout: ✅  │  │ stdout: ✅  │     │

title: ## Claude Code Review
text:
_##_ Claude Code Review

**Summary:** This refactoring improves the architecture by centralizing table lifecycle management in the `Agent` class. The changes are clean and well-tested.

**Issues Found:** None. PR looks good.

**Analysis:**

The refactoring moves MCP table creation/deletion from `AgentMCPClientStorage` to the `Agent` class constructor/destructor, which makes sense because:

1. **Better separation of concerns:** `AgentMCPClientStorage` is now purely a data access layer (CRUD operations), while `Agent` owns the lifecycle of all its tables
2. **Consistency:** The MCP table is now created/dropped alongside other agent tables (`cf_agents_state`, `cf_agents_schedules`, `cf_agents_queues`) in packages/agents/src/index.ts:434-444 and packages/agents/src/index.ts:1325
3. **Timing guarantees:** Table creation happens during `Agent` construction before `MCPClientManager` needs it, eliminating the race condition from the previous `create()` call
4. **Interface simplification:** Removes `create()` and `destroy()` methods from `MCPClientStorage` interface since storage implementations shouldn't manage their own schemas

**Testing coverage:** Excellent - the test suite in packages/agents/src/tests/mcp/client-manager.test.ts comprehensively covers MCP storage operations without needing the removed methods, confirming they were redundant.

_Originally posted by @claude in https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/666#issuecomment-3552194625_

### Problem Statement

Claude Code CLI is currently closed-source, while the main competitors (OpenAI Codex CLI, Google Gemini CLI) are open-source under Apache 2.0.

This creates several challenges:

1. **Issue burden without community contribution**: There are currently 5,600+ open issues, but the community cannot contribute fixes via pull requests. Maintainers bear the full cost of triaging and fixing, without the benefit of community contributions.

2. **Limited extensibility**: While MCP provides extension points, users cannot fix bugs, add features, or customize behavior at the core level.

3. **Transparency expectations**: Many users discover this repository expecting source code (see #333, #1645, #1789, #19073), leading to confusion and frustration.

I understand that in March 2025, the team mentioned they weren't ready to be "good public stewards yet" (#59). Nearly a year has passed, and I'd like to respectfully ask whether the situation has changed.

### Proposed Solution

Release Claude Code CLI under a permissive open-source license (e.g., Apache 2.0, MIT).

This would enable:

1. **Community bug fixes**: Users who encounter bugs can submit PRs instead of just filing issues. Maintainers review and merge, rather than investigating and implementing from scratch.

2. **Reduced triage burden**: Users who need a fix urgently can fork and fix locally, reducing pressure on the official issue queue.

3. **Ecosystem growth**: Third-party integrations, plugins, and forks can emerge, increasing Claude API adoption.

4. **Competitive parity**: Matching competitors' openness (Codex CLI, Gemini CLI are both Apache 2.0).

title: Claude Code: Errors of Judgment
text:
## Purpose

This issue tracks errors in judgment made by Claude Code during development of devlore-cli.

## Governing Principle

**This is a greenfield product. There is NO legacy. There are NO old APIs. There are NO previous versions to support.**

Any code that maintains backward compatibility, preserves old API signatures, accepts legacy formats, or provides fallbacks for old behavior **IS A CRITICAL BUG**.

---

## Label Definitions

### Area Labels

| Label | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Area:CLI` | Command-line interface |
| `Area:Architecture` | System architecture and design |
| `Area:Testing` | Test coverage and verification |
| `Area:ErrorHandling` | Error handling and propagation |
| `Area:CodeQuality` | Code quality and linting |
| `Area:Meta` | Process and tracking |
| `Area:Git` | Git operations |

### ClaudeJudgmentError Labels

| Label | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `ClaudeJudgmentError:Lie` | Claimed completion of work not done. An intentional falsehood - stating something was implemented, verified, or completed when it wasn't. |
| `ClaudeJudgmentError:FalseSuccess` | Code returns success (nil error) when the operation was not performed. Stubs that claim to succeed while doing nothing. |
| `ClaudeJudgmentError:IgnoredError` | Errors from operations silently discarded using `_, _ :=` when failure should be handled or reported. |
| `ClaudeJudgmentError:DesignDefect` | Architectural issues that should have been identified - disconnected systems, inconsistent patterns, missing integration. |
| `ClaudeJudgmentError:Incomplete` | Task claimed complete but not finished. Half-done operations presented as done. |

---

## Verification Checklist

Before completing any task:

- [ ] Grep for `legacy|backward|compat|deprecated` — remove all matches
- [ ] Verify no stub functions return success without implementation
- [ ] Verify removed comments have corresponding code removal
- [ ] Run tests to confirm rejection of old formats/signatures

## Summary

Extend the ticket output format so that tickets can be directly consumed by coding agents. Instead of just human-readable descriptions, tickets should include structured implementation specs: proposed UI changes, data model diffs, workflow descriptions, and file-level task breakdowns.

**Depends on:** #11 (Insight-to-Project bridge) — works best when tickets are evidence-grounded

## What to build

### 1. Extended ticket schema

Add optional agent-oriented fields to the `Ticket` model (or a related `TicketSpec` model):

- `proposedUIChanges` — Description of UI changes (component-level: "Add a toggle in the settings panel", "New onboarding wizard with 3 steps")
- `dataModelChanges` — Proposed schema or data model changes ("Add `onboardingCompleted` boolean to User model")
- `workflowChanges` — State machine or flow descriptions ("After signup, redirect to onboarding instead of dashboard")
- `fileHints` — Suggested files to modify (if connected to a codebase, or manual hints)
- `agentPrompt` — A pre-written prompt that could be copy-pasted into Cursor or Claude Code to implement this ticket

### 2. AI generates agent-ready specs

Update the `generateTickets` tool prompt to optionally produce these fields. Add a toggle or mode:
- **Human mode** (current) — tickets with descriptions, acceptance criteria, etc.
- **Agent mode** — tickets with the above + implementation specs

### 3. Export for agents

Add an export action per ticket or per project:
- **Copy as prompt** — Copies a well-structured prompt to clipboard that a coding agent can execute
- **Export as markdown** — Downloads a `.md` file with all tickets formatted for agent consumption
- **Export as JSON** — Structured format that could be consumed programmatically

### 4. Template for agent prompts

Design a prompt template that works well with Cursor/Claude Code:

## Task: [Ticket Title]

### Context

text:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing requests](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Aenhancement) and this feature hasn't been requested yet
- [x] This is a single feature request (not multiple features)

### Problem Statement

Claude Code (terminal) and Claude Cowork (desktop) are completely isolated. 
There is no way to programmatically trigger a Cowork task from Claude Code.

As a developer, I often need Claude Code's full terminal/coding power AND Cowork's desktop automation (computer use, file management, browser control via Claude in Chrome). Today I must manually switch between them and copy-paste context.

**Use cases that are currently impossible:**
- From Claude Code: "Run this UI test flow in Cowork using computer use"
- Chain a coding task in Claude Code → hand off to Cowork for visual verification
- Automate Cowork tasks in CI/CD or scripted workflows
- Use Playwright MCP in Claude Code to drive operations inside the Cowork app

### Proposed Solution

Any of these would solve the problem:

1. **A CLI command for Cowork** — e.g. `claude cowork "organize files in ~/Downloads"` that triggers a Cowork task from terminal
2. **A local API/IPC bridge** — Cowork exposes a localhost endpoint or Unix socket that Claude Code (or any MCP server) can call to submit tasks
3. **Shared MCP context** — Allow Claude Code and Cowork to share MCP servers and pass tasks between sessions
4. **An MCP server for Cowork itself** — So Claude Code can use Cowork as a "tool" (e.g., `cowork_run_task`, `cowork_get_result`)

### Alternative Solutions

_No response_

### Priority

High - Significant impact on productivity

### Feature Category

CLI commands and flags

### Use Case Example

Cowork and Claude Code are Anthropic's two most powerful agentic products. 
Right now they can't talk to each other. Bridging them would unlock developer workflows that neither can do alone — terminal-level coding 
automation + desktop-level comp

title: Browser Access for Kōan via Claude Code
text:
## Summary

Enable Kōan to interact with web browsers for E2E testing, documentation fetching, and web automation tasks.

## Context

Claude Code (2.0.73+) provides two mechanisms for browser access:

1. **`--chrome` flag** — Native Chrome integration requiring the Claude in Chrome extension
2. **MCP protocol** — Connect to browser automation servers (Playwright, Puppeteer) via Model Context Protocol

Both approaches have trade-offs. This issue analyzes use cases, security implications, and proposes an implementation path.

## Use Cases

### High Value

| Use Case | Description | Benefit |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| **E2E Testing** | Test frontend changes in real browser after writing code | Catch UI bugs before PR |
| **Screenshot Verification** | Capture screenshots of pages to verify layouts | Visual regression detection |
| **Console Error Detection** | Read browser console for JS errors/warnings | Frontend debugging |
| **Documentation Fetching** | Read live documentation from library websites | Up-to-date API info beyond knowledge cutoff |

### Medium Value

| Use Case | Description | Benefit |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| **Demo Recording** | Create GIF recordings of features | PR documentation |
| **Admin Dashboard Testing** | Verify admin panel changes work correctly | End-to-end verification |
| **Monitoring Checks** | Read Railway logs, Sentry issues via web UI | Proactive monitoring |

### Lower Priority / Riskier

| Use Case | Description | Concern |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| **Authenticated Web Apps** | Access Google Docs, Notion, etc. | Credential sharing risk |
| **Form Automation** | Fill out web forms automatically | Irreversible actions risk |

## Implementation Options

### Option A: `--chrome` Native (Desktop Only)

```yaml
# config.yaml
chrome:
  enabled: true
```

**Pros:**
- Zero setup, built into Claude Code
- Shares browser login state (can access authenticated sites)
- Native GIF recording

**Cons:**
- ❌

title: Native Claude Code hooks compatibility (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop)
text:
## Summary

OpenCode already has excellent Claude Code compatibility for rules (`CLAUDE.md`), skills (`~/.claude/skills/`), and can be disabled via `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE*` env vars. However, Claude Code's **hooks system** (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop` defined in `~/.claude/settings.json`) is not supported natively.

## Problem

Users who run both Claude Code and OpenCode maintain hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` that enforce guardrails:

- **PreToolUse** — Block dangerous operations (e.g., `git push` without tests, direct prod DB access, editing governed files without reading the architecture skill first)
- **PostToolUse** — Track state (e.g., mark that tests were run, mark that code files were edited)
- **Stop** — Verify the dev-loop SOP was followed before the agent stops (tests run, committed, deployed, QA'd)

These hooks are Python/bash scripts that receive JSON on stdin (`tool_name`, `tool_input`, `transcript_path`) and use exit codes to signal behavior (0=allow, 2=block+feedback via stderr).

Without native support, users must either:
1. Install `oh-my-opencode` (massive opinionated plugin that takes over the entire agent setup just for hook compat)
2. Write a custom bridge plugin (works for PreToolUse/PostToolUse but Stop hooks lose transcript access and can't re-activate the agent)

## Proposed Solution

Add native Claude Code hook execution, similar to how `CLAUDE.md` and skills are already handled:

1. **Read hooks from `~/.claude/settings.json`** (and `settings.local.json`) — parse the `hooks` object
2. **Map to OpenCode events:**
   - `PreToolUse` → `tool.execute.before` — transform tool names (`bash`→`Bash`, `edit`→`Edit`), pipe JSON stdin, respect exit code 2 as block
   - `PostToolUse` → `tool.execute.after` — same protocol, informational
   - `Stop` → `session.idle` — provide `transcript_path` with full session transcript (tool calls + assistant text), and critically: **if exit code 2, re-inject stderr as a prompt to continue** (this

title: Claude Code
text:
我来将这篇关于 Claude Code 的实战指南整理成一篇结构清晰、文笔流畅的中文文章。

---

# Claude Code 完全指南：一位七年资深工程师的实战心法

**作者背景**：Eyad Khrais，前 Amazon、Disney、Capital One 软件工程师，现为一家构建企业级 AI Agent 的初创公司 CTO。他经手的代码影响着数百万用户，构建的系统不允许有任何闪失。Claude Code 是他日常开发的核心工具。

以下是他在使用 Claude Code 构建大型企业复杂工作负载系统过程中，总结出的完整入门手册。

---

## 一、先思考，再动手

大多数人拿到 Claude Code 后的第一反应是立刻开始打字或语音输入。但这恰恰是最致命的错误。

**十次有十次，使用 Plan Mode（规划模式）的输出质量，都远胜于直接开口就来的方式。** 差距之大，超乎想象。

对于缺乏多年软件工程经验的人来说，"先思考"说起来容易做起来难。对此，作者给出两条建议：

1. **持续学习**。哪怕每次只学一点，完全不学只会让自己越来越被动。
2. **与 AI 深度对话**。向 ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude 详细描述你想构建的东西，询问各种系统设计方案，最终共同确定解决方案。注意，这是双向问答，不是单向灌输。

这个原则适用于所有场景——哪怕是总结邮件这种小事。让 Claude 写功能前，先想清楚架构；重构前，先设想最终形态；调试前，先梳理已知信息。**Plan Mode 里的信息越充分，输出质量就越高。**

规律始终如一：**先思考再打字，远胜于先打字再指望 Claude 自己琢磨。**

这就引出了架构的重要性。软件架构有点像只给人看输出结果，却不给过程——这留下了巨大的自由发挥空间，也正是 AI 生成代码的问题所在。

对比这两种指令：
- ❌ "给我做个认证系统"
- ✅ "基于现有 User 模型实现邮箱/密码认证，Session 存 Redis 24 小时过期，添加中间件保护 /api/protected 下的所有路由"

按两次 `Shift + Tab` 进入 Plan Mode。这 5 分钟的投入，能帮你省下数小时的调试时间。

---

## 二、CLAUDE.md：你的项目说明书

CLAUDE.md 是一个 Markdown 文件。Markdown 是 AI 模型处理得极好的文本格式，而 Claude 在这方面表现尤为出色。

每次启动 Claude Code 会话，Claude 首先读取的就是 CLAUDE.md。文件中的每条指令都会塑造它处理你项目的方式——这相当于 Claude 在每次对话前必读的入职材料。

大多数人要么完全忽略它，要么塞满垃圾信息让 Claude 变得更糟。**信息过多或过少，都会降低模型输出质量。**

### 撰写 CLAUDE.md 的黄金法则：

**1. 保持简洁**
Claude 一次只能可靠遵循约 150-200 条指令，而 Claude Code 的系统提示已经占用了约 50 条。每条新增指令都在争夺注意力。如果你的 CLAUDE.md 像小说一样长，Claude 会随机忽略部分内容，而你根本不知道忽略了哪些。

**2. 项目特异性**
别解释什么是 components 文件夹——Claude 知道。要写的是那些"奇怪的东西"：真正重要的 bash 命令、你的工作流细节。

**3. 说明原因，而非仅陈述事实**
Claude 在这方面有点像人类。给出指令背后的理由，它执行起来会比单纯被告知"做什么"更好。
- 一般："使用 TypeScript 严格模式"
- 更好："使用 TypeScript 严格模式，因为我们曾因隐式 any 类型引发过生产环境 Bug"

**4. 持续更新**
工作时按 `#` 键，Claude 会自动向 CLAUDE.md 添加指令。如果你发现自己在重复纠正 Claude 同一个问题超过两次，这就是该写入文件的信号。随着时间推移，CLAUDE.md 会成为代码库实际运作方式的活文档。

> **糟糕的 CLAUDE.md** 像写给新员工的文档；**优秀的 CLAUDE.md** 像写给明天就会失忆的自己的笔记。

---

## 三、上下文窗口的陷阱

以 Opus 4.5 为例，它拥有 20 万 token 的上下文窗口。但大多数人没意识到：**模型在达到 100% 之前很久就开始衰退了**（API 调用与桌面应用的表现略有差异）。

大约在 **20-40% 的上下文使用率**时，输出质量就开始下滑，即使不明显。如果你经历过 Claude Code 压缩上下文后仍然给出糟糕输出，

DevContainer 設定を manifest.toml から自動生成し、Claude Code や Cursor が安全に実行できる環境を提供する。

title: Direct LLM export — send review to Claude Code, Copilot, etc. without copy-paste
text:
## Problem

Today, exporting a review requires **3 steps**: Export → Copy to clipboard → Paste into your LLM. This breaks the flow, especially when iterating multiple times on the same review.

## Proposal

Add a **"Send to…"** action that pushes the structured review payload directly into the target LLM — zero clipboard, zero tab switching.

## Two integration modes

### 1. Terminal — spin up & pipe

Sieve opens (or reuses) a VS Code terminal and injects the command with the prompt:

| CLI | Generated command |
|-----|-----------------|
| **Claude Code** | `claude --prompt "$(cat /tmp/sieve-review.md)"` |
| **Aider** | `/ask < /tmp/sieve-review.md` in the active session |
| **Open Interpreter** | Pipe stdin into the session |
| **Codex CLI** | Prompt injection via stdin |

The user sees the terminal open, the command run, and the response stream in live. Nothing to copy-paste.

### 2. VS Code extensions — direct command

For LLMs integrated as extensions, Sieve uses their API/commands:

| Extension | Method |
|-----------|--------|
| **Copilot Chat** | VS Code Chat API |
| **Cursor AI** | Composer input injection |
| **Cline** | Extension-to-extension command |
| **Continue** | Extension API |

## UX flow

1. User presses `S` (Send)
2. QuickPick: **"Send review to…"** → lists detected targets
3. Sieve formats the payload for the selected target
4. **Terminal**: opens a terminal, writes a temp file, runs the command
5. **Extension**: sends directly via the extension's API

## Auto-detection

Sieve automatically detects:
- CLIs in PATH (`claude`, `aider`, `interpreter`, `codex`)
- Installed extensions (Copilot, Cline, Continue)

Only available targets show up in the picker.

## Settings

```jsonc
{
  "sieve.sendTargets": {
    "claudeCode": { "autoDetect": true },
    "aider": { "autoDetect": true },
    "copilotChat": { "autoDetect": true }
  }
}
```

## Out of scope

- Receiving LLM responses back into Sieve (bidirectional) → separate issue
- MCP server integration

title: Create Claude Code plugin marketplace
text:
Since the introduction of [plugins in Claude Code](https://claude.com/blog/claude-code-plugins), several MCP servers began being distributed as part of/exposed through Claude Code plugins for more convenient access to said MCP servers.

[Creating and distributing a Claude Code plugin marketplace](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/plugin-marketplaces) would be a great quality-of-life enhancement for the Astro Docs MCP server, making it easier for Claude Code users to connect to it, similar to the convenient deep links already available for Cursor and Visual Studio Code.

In addition to the above, I find that creating a plugin for Astro would be especially valuable as Claude Code plugins can also bundle [LSP servers](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins#add-lsp-servers-to-your-plugin) alongside MCP servers. As an example, the [Svelte plugin](https://github.com/sveltejs/mcp) does exactly this. It would make a lot of sense for Astro to do the same, combining the Astro Docs MCP server (in this repo) with the Astro language server ([`@astrojs/language-server`](https://github.com/withastro/astro/tree/main/packages/language-tools/language-server)) into one plugin. This would give Claude Code users:

- Access to the latest Astro docs via MCP
- Code intelligence for `.astro` files via LSP

The end result is that Claude Code users would be able to set up everything with two commands:

```text
/plugin marketplace add withastro/docs-mcp
/plugin install astro
```

This replaces the current manual setup of running `claude mcp add --transport http "Astro docs" https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp`, while providing more functionality.

Additionally, plugin installations are tracked in the project’s `.claude/settings.json` under `enabledPlugins`. This means a team can commit that file to their repo so that every contributor who opens the project in Claude Code automatically has the Astro Docs MCP server available; no per-user setup required.

title: Test with multiple MCP clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT)
text:
## Problem

We currently only test our MCP server with Claude Code. Different AI clients handle tool selection, parameter passing, and response parsing differently. A tool that works perfectly in Claude Code may fail in ChatGPT, Cursor, or Claude Desktop due to differences in:

- **Tool selection heuristics** — each client weighs tool names, descriptions, and schemas differently
- **Parameter generation** — some clients are more aggressive with optional parameters, others skip them
- **Response interpretation** — structured vs text content handling varies
- **Batch/streaming support** — not all clients support SSE or JSON-RPC batching
- **Annotation handling** — some clients use `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` for auto-approval, others ignore them

From [Speakeasy's controlled experiment](https://www.speakeasy.com/mcp/tool-design/less-is-more):
> Models behave differently with the same tool set. What works for GPT-5 may fail for Claude 4.5, and vice versa.

From [GitHub Copilot's findings](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/how-were-making-github-copilot-smarter-with-fewer-tools/):
> Tool performance varied by 2-5 percentage points between GPT-5 and Sonnet 4.5 on the same benchmarks.

## Proposed Testing Matrix

### MCP Clients to Test

| Client | Transport | Priority | Notes |
|--------|-----------|----------|-------|
| Claude Code (CLI) | Streamable HTTP | ✅ Current | Primary development client |
| Claude Desktop | Streamable HTTP | High | Most popular MCP client |
| Cursor | Streamable HTTP | High | Popular AI IDE |
| Windsurf | Streamable HTTP | Medium | Growing AI IDE |
| ChatGPT | Streamable HTTP | Medium | Different model, different tool-calling behavior |
| Continue.dev | Streamable HTTP | Low | Open-source IDE extension |

### Test Scenarios per Client

#### 1. Discovery & Selection
- [ ] Agent correctly identifies available tools from `tools/list`
- [ ] Agent selects appropriate tool for natural language requests
- [ ] Agent handles tool descrip

title: Ship IntentGuard as a native hook for Claude Code, Copilot, and Cursor
text:
### Why
This is the single most important strategic issue.

Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor all now ship native hooks (PreToolUse/PostToolUse). Instead of competing with hooks, IntentGuard should **become the brain that hooks call**. This flips the competitive threat into a distribution channel.

### What
Create a CLI command `intent-guard evaluate` that:
- Reads hook input JSON from stdin (tool name, arguments, context)
- Runs the full IntentGuard evaluation pipeline (static + semantic)
- Exits 0 (allow) or 1 (block), with JSON verdict on stdout

Ship ready-to-use hook configs for all three platforms.

### Acceptance Criteria
- `intent-guard evaluate --policy <path>` CLI command
- Reads stdin JSON matching each platform's hook input format
- Returns structured JSON verdict on stdout
- Exit code 0 = allow, 1 = block
- Example hook configs shipped in `hooks/` directory:
  - `hooks/claude-code/settings.json` — PreToolUse command hook calling intent-guard
  - `hooks/copilot/hooks.json` — preToolUse hook
  - `hooks/cursor/hooks.json` — pre-tool hook
- Documentation: "Use IntentGuard with Claude Code in 2 minutes"
- Tests: end-to-end hook simulation

### Strategic context
- Hooks are commoditized static interception. IntentGuard adds semantic intelligence on top.
- IntentGuard's externalized policy is immune to CVE-2025-59536-class supply chain attacks (malicious repo configs auto-executing). Blog/README should highlight this.
- This is how IntentGuard reaches developers who would otherwise just use built-in hooks.

Supersedes #22 (non-MCP agent support) with a pragmatic approach.

title: No support for non-MCP agents (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor direct tool use)
text:
### Why
IntentGuard only works as an MCP stdio proxy. But the biggest AI coding tools — Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor — primarily use **direct tool calls** (bash, file edit, etc.) that are NOT routed through MCP servers. The README shows Claude Code integration via MCP server config, but Claude Code's most dangerous tools (bash execution, direct file writes) bypass MCP entirely.

This means IntentGuard **cannot guard the most dangerous attack surface** in the tools it claims to support.

### What's needed
- A process-level interception layer (e.g., eBPF, LD_PRELOAD, FUSE filesystem, or ptrace-based) for file/exec operations
- Or: SDK hooks that agent frameworks can call before tool execution (pre-tool middleware)
- Or: A VS Code / IDE extension that intercepts tool calls at the editor level

### Enterprise impact
If you pitch 'we guard your AI coding agents' but can only guard MCP filesystem server calls while Claude Code's `bash` tool can `rm -rf /` unimpeded, the product has a critical gap in its value proposition.

title: MCP server — query VectorLens from Claude Code / Cursor
text:
## Why this matters

VectorLens captures rich attribution data but you can only view it in the browser. If VectorLens exposed an MCP server, Claude Code or Cursor could query it mid-conversation: "what hallucinated in my last run?" or "which chunk had the highest attribution score?"

## Proposed interface

```python

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("VectorLens")

@mcp.tool()
def get_latest_session() -> dict: ...

@mcp.tool()
def get_hallucinations(session_id: str) -> list[dict]: ...

@mcp.tool()
def get_chunk_attributions(session_id: str) -> list[dict]: ...

@mcp.tool()  
def get_groundedness_score(session_id: str) -> float: ...
```

Start alongside the dashboard: `vectorlens.serve(mcp=True)`

## Implementation notes

- Use `fastmcp` package (`pip install fastmcp`)
- MCP server runs on stdio (standard MCP transport)
- Reads from the same in-memory session bus
- Add to Claude Code config: `{"mcpServers": {"vectorlens": {"command": "python", "args": ["-m", "vectorlens.mcp_server"]}}}`

title: U+23FA (⏺) ambiguous-width character causes cursor misalignment in Claude Code UI
text:
### Checklist

- [x] Using latest version on the [App Store](http://itunes.apple.com/app/id1156707581)
- [x] Read the [docs](http://blink.sh/docs/)
- [x] Searched for [existing GitHub issues](https://github.com/blinksh/blink/issues)

### Configuration

- Blink Shell 18.5
- iPadOS 26
- iPad Pro 11-inch M4
- Connected via SSH to Mac Studio
- Running Claude Code in the remote session
- Font tested: Pragmata Pro (default), JetBrains Mono Nerd Font — issue persists with both
- TERM: xterm-256color

### Describe the bug

Claude Code’s default UI uses U+23FA (⏺ BLACK CIRCLE FOR RECORD) as a status indicator in its terminal interface. This character is classified as **East Asian Ambiguous** width in Unicode (UAX #11), meaning the terminal must decide whether to treat it as 1 or 2 cells wide.

Blink’s hterm rendering engine appears to calculate a different width for this character than Claude Code expects, causing a persistent cursor misalignment artifact — the character renders as a “half disc” and subsequent text on the line is shifted. This is purely cosmetic but is visible during every interaction with Claude Code.

**Root cause:** hterm does not expose a user-configurable setting for ambiguous-width character handling (unlike iTerm2’s “Treat ambiguous-width characters as wide” toggle, or similar options in mintty and Apple Terminal.app). The width is determined by hterm’s internal `wcwidth` table, and there is no way for users to override it.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Open Blink Shell and connect via SSH to a remote machine
1. Run Claude Code (`claude` CLI)
1. Observe the ⏺ (U+23FA) status indicator in Claude Code’s UI
1. The character renders incorrectly — appears as a half-width glyph with subsequent text misaligned

**Expected behavior:**

The ⏺ character should render at a consistent width that matches the cursor positioning assumed by the application, with no visual artifacts or text misalignment.

**What I’ve tried:**

- Switching fonts (Pragmata Pro → JetBrain

2. **Claude Code Scheduled Tasks** - 为 Claude Code 添加定时任务能力
3. **Context.dev** - Web 抓取和理解的统一 API
4. **Edgee Claude Code Compression** - 压缩 Claude Code 上下文

**趋势分析：**
- AI Coding Agent 工具链快速成熟（Claude Code、Cursor、GitHub Copilot 等）
- 每个工具都有自己的优势场景
- 但缺乏跨工具协作机制，开发者被锁定在单一生态

**痛点：**
- 不同 AI Agent 无法共享上下文和知识
- 项目在不同工具间切换成本高
- 缺乏统一的工作流编排和监控
- 每个工具的输出格式不统一

## 解决方案
构建 **AgentFlow** - 一个 AI Agent 工作流协作平台：

### 核心功能
1. **统一上下文管理**
   - 跨 Agent 的项目上下文同步
   - 会话历史和知识库共享
   - 统一的文件变更追踪

2. **智能任务路由**
   - 根据任务类型自动选择最合适的 Agent
   - 支持多 Agent 协作（Claude Code 写核心逻辑，Cursor 优化 UI，Copilot 补全测试）
   - 任务依赖管理和并行执行

3. **工作流可视化**
   - 类似 Bench 的审计追踪，但跨所有 Agent
   - 统一的时间线和决策记录
   - Agent 间交接点的清晰标注

4. **标准化输出**
   - 统一的 PR 格式（整合不同 Agent 的贡献）
   - 标准化的代码审查意见
   - 自动生成 CHANGELOG

### 技术方案
- **协议层**: 定义 Agent 间通信协议（基于 LSP 或自定义 JSON-RPC）
- **适配器**: 为每个主流 Agent 开发适配器
- **编排引擎**: 基于 DAG 的任务调度
- **存储层**: Git-based 知识库 + 向量数据库

### MVP 功能
1. Claude Code + Cursor 双 Agent 支持
2. 项目级上下文同步
3. 简单的任务分配 UI
4. 统一的变更历史视图

## 可行性
⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

**优势：**
- 市场需求明确（开发者使用多个 AI 工具已成常态）
- 技术可行（各 Agent 都有 CLI/API）
- 竞争对手少（目前都是单一生态解决方案）

**挑战：**
- 需要获得各 Agent 厂商支持或逆向工程
- Agent 能力差异大，编排逻辑复杂
- 性能开销（多个 Agent 同时运行）

**建议路线：**
1. 先做 Claude Code + Cursor 集成（两个最流行的独立 Agent）
2. 开源核心，吸引社区贡献其他 Agent 适配器
3. 商业化方向：团队协作、高级编排、企业版

## 参考
- [Bench for Claude Code](https://www.producthunt.com/products/bench-for-claude-code) - 会话追踪
- [Claude Code Scheduled Tasks](https://www.producthunt.com/products/claude-code-scheduled-tasks) - 任务调度
- [Context.dev](https://www.producthunt.com/products/context-dev) - 统一 API
- [Cursor](https://www.producthunt.com/products/cursor) - AI Code Editor
- [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) - 代码补全

## 市场时机
- AI Coding Agent 市场在 2026 年进入成熟期
- 开发者平均使用 2-3 个 AI 编程工具
- 缺乏统一的最佳实践和工具链
- 这是建立标准的窗口期

title: M17: prismkv-mcp — MCP server wrapper for Claude Code/Cursor/Gemini integration
text:
## Summary

Make PrismKV frictionless to adopt in AI coding tools by shipping an MCP (Model Context Protocol)
server wrapper. `pip install prismkv[mcp]` → instant compressed KV cache for any MCP-compatible
client.

## Motivation

> "Being able to tack this onto popular coding tools like Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor and others
> would be beneficial — if we want people to test this, they need it to be frictionless."

MCP is the standard protocol for tool/resource injection in Claude Code, Cursor, Continue.dev, and
others. A PrismKV MCP server means any developer can try compressed KV caching in their existing
workflow without changing model code.

## Proposed Design

### `src/prismkv/mcp/server.py`

```python
# prismkv-mcp: MCP server exposing PrismKVCache as a shared resource
#
# Usage:
#   pip install prismkv[mcp]
#   prismkv-mcp --model gpt2 --bits 4 --port 8080
#
# Claude Code / Cursor config:
#   { "mcpServers": { "prismkv": { "command": "prismkv-mcp", "args": ["--bits", "4"] } } }
```

### MCP Resources

- `prismkv://status` — current compression stats (bits/dim, RMSE, memory saved)
- `prismkv://config` — current PrismKVConfig per layer
- `prismkv://benchmark` — run quick benchmark and return results

### MCP Tools

- `compress_kv` — compress a KV cache tensor, return compressed size
- `decompress_kv` — decompress and return FP16 tensor
- `set_bits` — change bits/dim at runtime

## Install Extra

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[project.optional-dependencies]
mcp = ["mcp>=1.0", "uvicorn"]
```

## CLI Entry Point

```toml
[project.scripts]
prismkv-mcp = "prismkv.mcp.server:main"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pip install prismkv[mcp]` installs MCP server
- [ ] `prismkv-mcp --bits 4` starts a working MCP server
- [ ] Works with Claude Code MCP configuration
- [ ] `prismkv://status` resource returns compression stats
- [ ] `compress_kv` / `decompress_kv` tools round-trip correctly
- [ ] Tests: `tests/test_mcp_server.py` (mock MCP client)
- [ ] README updated with MCP

title: Support Claude Code and GH Copilot CLI via LiteLLM translation proxy
text:
Currently, the `opencode-rl` script supports OpenCode and Goose CLI seamlessly since they work with OpenAI-compatible endpoints natively out-of-the-box. 

However, Claude Code strictly expects the Anthropic `Messages API` schema (`/v1/messages`), while RamaLama uses `llama.cpp` to expose an OpenAI-compatible schema (`/v1/chat/completions`). GitHub Copilot CLI is also currently hardcoded to Microsoft/GitHub backend servers for standard CLI commands and doesn't support generic endpoints.

To support Claude Code (and potentially GH Copilot in the future if they open up CLI tooling), we should integrate a translation proxy like **LiteLLM**. 

**Proposed Solution:**
* Add an optional flag/workflow in `opencode-rl` to spin up a lightweight, stateless `LiteLLM` container alongside the `ramalama` container.
* The `LiteLLM` proxy would translate the incoming Anthropic requests from Claude Code into OpenAI requests for RamaLama.
* The script would export `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing to the LiteLLM proxy port when launching Claude Code.

title: Claude Code plugin/marketplace compatibility
text:
# Claude Code plugin/marketplace compatibility

## Problem

In this document, a plugin manifest is a JSON file named `plugin.json` that describes components of a software plugin. A skill catalog is the collection of skills that DecafClaw discovers and registers for agent use.

Anthropic Claude Code plugins follow a structure with a `plugin.json` manifest and skill directories. DecafClaw cannot currently load or discover skills packaged as Claude Code plugins. Users who clone plugin repositories cannot use their skills in DecafClaw without manual reorganization.

## Intended Result

When a user configures a plugin directory, `discover_skills()` must detect the Claude Code `plugin.json` manifest. DecafClaw must parse declared skill paths in the manifest. DecafClaw must register all valid declared skills into the skill catalog. If a plugin declares native tools, DecafClaw must register those tools with the appropriate trust tier.

## Proposed Changes

We propose the following technical changes:

- In `src/decafclaw/skills/__init__.py`, update `_iter_skill_dirs` or add a manifest scanner for `plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
- Parse the plugin manifest JSON to find declared skill directories and tool definitions.
- For each declared skill path, validate the `SKILL.md` file using `validate_skill_md`.
- Register each valid skill as a `SkillInfo` instance in the skill catalog.
- Apply the trust tier of the parent scan entry to the discovered plugin skills.

## Boundaries and Exclusions

- We do not implement Claude Code lifecycle hooks.
- We do not implement Claude Code custom slash commands.
- We do not implement subagent definitions in this issue.
- We do not integrate remote marketplace registry APIs.
- Discovery applies only to locally installed directories in configured skill paths.

- Add unit tests in `tests/test_skills.py`.
- Make sure that tests verify discovery of skills from a mock directory containing `plugi

title: Claude Code Auto Mode Classifier Compatibility Issue
text:
# Claude Code Auto Mode Classifier Compatibility Issue

## Problem Description

When using CC Switch's Anthropic Base URL proxy (e.g., `http://127.0.0.1:15721`), Claude Code's Auto Mode classifier fails with the following error:

```
The auto mode classifier is temporarily unavailable, so Bash cannot be used right now. (dacEnabled=n/a, hasExtraBody=false)
```

This results in:
- ❌ Bash/WebFetch tools being blocked
- ⚠️ Write/Edit tools working intermittently
- ✅ Read/Grep/Glob tools working normally
- ✅ MCP tools working normally (independent permission path)

## Root Cause Analysis

Through systematic debugging, we identified that the local proxy intercepts Claude Code's API requests to `api.anthropic.com`, but the proxy implementation is incompatible with the Auto Mode classifier service's backend connection requirements.

**Key diagnostic insight**:
- `curl` tests show normal TLS handshake and HTTP 405 response (expected)
- Claude Code's classifier still fails with `dacEnabled=n/a`
- This is because `curl` uses system proxy, while Claude Code uses CC Switch's Base URL proxy

**Network path difference**:
| Tool | Network Path |
|------|-------------|
| `curl` | System proxy (Clash Verge HTTP/HTTPS port) |
| Claude Code | CC Switch Base URL (`http://127.0.0.1:15721`) |

## Reproduction Steps

1. Configure CC Switch with Anthropic Base URL: `http://127.0.0.1:15721`
2. Start Claude Code in Auto Mode
3. Attempt to use Bash tool: `echo "test"`
4. Observe error: `dacEnabled=n/a`

## Workaround

**Current solution**: Disable CC Switch's Anthropic Base URL proxy.

After disabling the proxy and restarting Claude Code session, the classifier immediately recovers.

## Suggested Fix

It would be helpful if CC Switch could:
1. Document the incompatibility with Claude Code's Auto Mode classifier
2. Provide a configuration option to bypass the classifier service endpoint
3. Or investigate why the local proxy breaks the classifier's backend connection

## Environment

- Claude Co

text:
## Summary

Hermes WebUI already imports sessions from the Hermes CLI agent (reads `~/.hermes/state.db` via `get_cli_sessions()` in `api/models.py`). The same pattern could be extended to import read-only session history from other AI agents — Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, and others — giving users a unified place to browse all their past AI conversations.

This was requested by a community member who has years of sessions across multiple tools and no good way to review them.

## Agents and their storage formats

| Agent | Format | Default location |
|-------|--------|-----------------|
| Claude Code | JSONL per project (`messages` array with `role`/`content`) | `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/` |
| OpenAI Codex | JSON sessions | `~/.codex/` |
| Cursor | SQLite (`workspaceStorage`) | `~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/workspaceStorage/` |
| Windsurf | SQLite (similar to Cursor/VSCode) | `~/Library/Application Support/Windsurf/` |
| Aider | Markdown chat logs | Per-repo `.aider.chat.history.md` |

Claude Code is the highest-priority target — it's the most common overlap with Hermes users and the format is straightforward JSONL.

### Phase 1 — Claude Code import (well-scoped, high value)

Add a `get_claude_code_sessions()` function in `api/models.py` mirroring `get_cli_sessions()`:

1. Scan `~/.claude/projects/*/` for JSONL session files
2. Parse `role`/`content` message arrays (same shape as Hermes messages)
3. Surface them in the sidebar under a `cli_session: true` flag and a `source: "claude_code"` tag, read-only
4. Show source badge in the session header (similar to how CLI sessions are currently distinguished)

No write operations — import is purely read-only. Sessions are never modified or deleted.

### Phase 2 — Generic import endpoint

A `POST /api/import/session` endpoint accepting a standard JSON payload:

## Context
Phase 1 hero feature — Claude Code support transforms ClawForge from "OpenClaw tool" to "AI agent governance platform."

## Task
Build `packages/claude-code/` adapter using Claude Code's HTTP hooks system.

### Hook mappings
| ClawForge Capability | Claude Code Mechanism |
|-----|------|
| Tool policy enforcement | `PreToolUse` hook → core policy engine → `permissionDecision: "deny"` |
| Audit logging | `PostToolUse` + `PostToolUseFailure` hooks |
| Kill switch | `PreToolUse` hook blocking ALL tools |
| DLP scanning | `PreToolUse` hook scans `tool_input` params |
| Session tracking | `SessionStart` / `SessionEnd` hooks |

### Deliverables
- `packages/claude-code/hooks/` — PreToolUse, PostToolUse HTTP hook handlers
- `packages/claude-code/settings/` — managed settings generator
- Hook handlers call `@clawforgeai/core` policy engine

title: Help wanted: Claude Code testers
text:
mcp-clipboard was built for Claude Code — it works around the [terminal padding bug](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/4686) that corrupts long commands when you copy them from Claude Code's output. If you use Claude Code, even 10 minutes of testing would be a huge help.

### Setup

```bash
claude mcp add clipboard -- uvx mcp-clipboard
```

That's it. Claude Code will discover the tools automatically.

### Tests

#### Clipboard padding workaround

1. Ask Claude Code to generate a long shell command (something with pipes, quotes, or flags)
2. Instead of copying from the terminal, say: **"Copy that command to my clipboard"**
3. Paste into your terminal — verify it's clean (no leading spaces, no hard line breaks)

#### Core functionality

- [ ] Copy plain text → "read my clipboard" → returns the text
- [ ] Copy cells from a spreadsheet → "paste my clipboard" → returns a Markdown table
- [ ] Copy a URL → "what's on my clipboard?" → returns the URL cleanly
- [ ] Copy some code → "read what I copied" → returns in a code block
- [ ] Copy an image → "paste my clipboard" → Claude can see and describe the image
- [ ] "Copy this to my clipboard: hello world" → verify it lands on your clipboard

#### Auto-copy behavior (optional)

Add this to your `CLAUDE.md`:

```
When you produce a shell command for the user to run, also copy it to the clipboard using clipboard_copy.
```

- [ ] Verify Claude Code automatically copies commands without being asked

#### Debug logging

If something doesn't work:

```bash
MCP_CLIPBOARD_DEBUG=1 claude
```

Or run the server standalone:

```bash
uvx mcp-clipboard --debug
```

### Platforms

- **Linux (Wayland)**: Tested — this is the primary dev platform
- **Linux (X11)**: Unit tested, unverified on live hardware
- **macOS**: Implemented, untested (see #5)
- **Windows**: Implemented, untested (see #5)

Comment on this issue with:
- Your OS and platform (e.g., macOS 15.3, Fedora 43 Wayland, Windows 11)
- Claude Code

title: Unified AI Router — multi-provider architecture (BYOK + Ollama + Claude Code + Copilot)
text:
# Unified AI Router — Architecture & Implementation Plan

## TL;DR

Lokus needs AI features (editor commands, meeting summary, plugin SDK, future agents). Today only the meeting overlay calls AI, through a hardcoded OpenAI/Anthropic switch in `src/services/ai-provider.js`.

We want to support **four backends** without writing four pipelines:

1. **BYOK** — user-provided API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, etc.)
2. **Ollama** — local models, no auth, runs on `localhost:11434`
3. **Claude Code** — reuse the user's existing Claude Pro/Max subscription via the OAuth token Claude Code's CLI stores at `~/.config/claude/credentials.json`
4. **GitHub Copilot** — reuse the user's Copilot subscription via device-code OAuth

Solution: build **one router** on top of the [Vercel AI SDK](https://github.com/vercel/ai) (Apache 2.0). Every backend becomes a `LanguageModelV1` adapter. All call sites in Lokus speak one canonical request/response shape.

ChatGPT Plus and Gemini Advanced subscriptions are explicitly **out of scope** — neither has a stable local credential file or third-party OAuth, only browser cookies (fragile + ToS violation).

---

## Why This Matters

Without a router we will:

- Write streaming, error handling, secure-storage, and cancellation logic four times
- Couple each AI surface (editor / meeting / plugins) to a specific provider
- Block plugin authors from using AI without their own keys
- Have no clean path to add a 5th provider next quarter

With the router:

- One `EditorAPI.ai.stream({ profile, messages })` works for every plugin and surface
- Adding a new provider = one Rust adapter + npm install
- Users pick **profiles** (`fast` / `smart` / `private` / `vision`) — not vendors
- Credentials live in one vault (`secure_storage.rs`), not scattered across modules

---

## Current State (Audit)

| Layer | What exists | What's missing |
|---|---|---|
| `src/services/ai-provider.js` | `createLLMClient` with hardcoded OpenAI + Anthropic, lokus-proxy mode

title: Fix: fake cursor position wrong in TUI apps (Claude Code, vim, etc.)
text:
## Problem

The web UI always renders a fake blinking cursor `█` at the very end of terminal content. This is correct for normal shell prompts (cursor IS at the end), but wrong for TUI applications like Claude Code, vim, htop, and less that use alternate screen buffers — the real cursor is elsewhere on screen, making the fake cursor misleading.

## Root Cause

- `iterm.js:getContent()` fetches plain text via AppleScript `contents of s` — no cursor position info available
- `App.tsx:884` hardcodes `█` at the end of all content regardless of actual cursor position
- iTerm2's AppleScript API does NOT expose `cursor row`/`cursor column`

## Fix

Layered detection approach:

### Layer 1 (definitive): iTerm2 `is at shell prompt` property
- `true` → show fake cursor at end (correct for shell)
- `false` → hide fake cursor (TUI app running)
- `null` (Shell Integration not installed) → fall to Layer 2

### Layer 2 (fallback): Content-based heuristics
- Line count significantly exceeds terminal rows → scrolling shell → show cursor
- Content fills the screen with dense output → likely TUI → hide cursor
- Default → show cursor (wrong cursor > no cursor)

### Debounce
Only change cursor visibility after 2 consecutive agreeing decisions to prevent flicker during transitions.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `server/iterm.js` | New `getSessionInfo(sessionId)` method — queries `rows`, `columns`, `is at shell prompt` via AppleScript |
| `server/index.js` | Extended `streamContent()` to include `meta: { rows, columns, atShellPrompt, lineCount }` in content events |
| `client/src/App.tsx` | Added `shouldShowCursor()` helper with layered detection, debounce logic, conditional cursor rendering |

## Verification

39 assertions across 3 test suites, all passing:

| Test Suite | Assertions | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `shouldShowCursor` pure function (unit) | 18 | ✅ All passed |
| `getSessionInfo()` against live iTerm2 (integration) | 9 | ✅ All passed |
| Server `stre

title: [Feature]: Add Claude Code and Cursor hooks for automatic security context injection
text:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Right now, the repo relies on MCP to provide security context and requirements, but if that context is only loaded through an explicit trigger, it can arrive too late in the code-generation flow. In fast AI-assisted coding sessions, that means code may be generated before the right security constraints are in place, which can lead to inconsistent enforcement of security requirements and missed safeguards.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like the repo to support Claude Code hooks and Cursor hooks as an additional trigger layer, while keeping MCP as the source of security context.

The hooks should:
- detect when code is about to be generated,
- identify the relevant task, file type, or request,
- request the appropriate security context from MCP,
- inject that context into the AI workflow before code is produced.

This would preserve the existing MCP behavior while making security guidance available automatically at the right point in the workflow for both Claude Code and Cursor users.

title: Claude Code: installers write the Agents-Core routing reminder to `<profile>/memory/`, which Claude Code never loads
text:
## Problem

The original report (2026-04-11, titled "Common Claude code instruction and memory won't route to Agents MCP") has no body. It was filed 43 minutes after PR #27 ("Configures Claude global routing memory") merged. That PR made `scripts/init_repo.sh` write a Claude Code memory reminder next to the managed `CLAUDE.md` routing section. *Assumption:* the issue is about that instructions-plus-memory setup not making Claude Code call Agents-Core.

**The instruction half has not reproduced since.** My Claude Code transcripts from two other local repositories, whose own `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` have no Agents-Core section, show unprompted `route_and_load` calls on 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-26. The managed section alone was enough. Both calls were protocol 1 calls (no `protocol_version` argument). Protocol 1 required routing before every answer and was removed by PR #101 on 2026-09-29. Protocol 2 routes only when no role is active or the task needs another specialist (`scripts/templates/routing-protocol-core.md`, "Decide locally before each answer"). No protocol 2 session outside this repository has been checked yet, so the acceptance criteria include one such check.

**The memory half is still a defect.** The reminder is written to a directory Claude Code does not read:

- `scripts/init_repo.sh` (Claude Code block, step 3, `CLAUDE_MEMORY_DIR="$CLAUDE_CODE_DIR/memory"`) asks a separate "Allow?" question once the managed `CLAUDE.md` section is configured (auto-accepted with `--yes`, which `install.sh` passes), then runs `scripts/_helpers/migrate_routing_memory.py`. The helper creates or migrates `<profile>/memory/feedback_agents_core_routing.md` and adds or replaces its line in `<profile>/memory/MEMORY.md`. `<profile>` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude` (`client_home` in `src/client_paths.py`).
- `scripts/install_instructions.py` (`install_claude_instructions`, via `migrate(..., existing_only=True)`) and `scripts/init_repo.bat` (`--existing-only`) run the same help

title: Add client setup and compatibility validation for Claude Code, Codex, VS Code Copilot, and Cursor
text:
## Goal
Add documented setup examples and compatibility validation for using the appropriate `memory-mcp` plugin/profile from Claude Code, Codex, VS Code + GitHub Copilot, and Cursor while connecting to the separately running Docker-backed `memory-mcp` service.

## Background / Context
`memory-mcp` should work outside the `ai-os` application for common agent clients. The target clients are:

- Claude Code
- Codex
- VS Code + GitHub Copilot
- Cursor

The Docker-backed memory service/backend is managed separately. Client setup docs should not imply that each plugin launches or embeds the backend/database. The host-specific MCP/plugin configuration should connect to the already-running service and select the appropriate profile.

Each host may support MCP configuration differently, and those details can change over time. The repo should provide host-specific setup docs, examples, known limitations, and a repeatable smoke-test checklist.

This story depends on or complements the profile-specific MCP plugin launcher story. The expected default for external coding/planning/review agents is the compact `agent` profile, not the richer `ai-os` profile.

## Problem
A generic MCP setup guide is not enough. If setup is vague, agents may:

- Configure a plugin before the Docker service is running.
- Start the wrong profile.
- Use broad graph retrieval by default.
- Miss memory entirely because the client config path, command shape, service URL, or service health state is wrong.
- Get access to mutation/admin tools unnecessarily.
- Fail silently when the Docker service, database, or migrations are unavailable.
- Use outdated client-specific MCP instructions.

## Desired behavior
The repo should contain host-specific docs and validation steps showing how to configure the plugin/profile for each target client and how to verify the separately managed service is available first.

Each host guide should answer:

- How do I start/verify the Docker-backed `memory-mcp` service separately

title: Expose plugin-registered tools as MCP tools for Cursor/Claude Code adapters
text:
## Feature Request

Plugin tools registered via `agent.tools.register` and `ctx.tools.register()` are not available as native tools in Cursor and Claude Code adapters. Agents using these adapters cannot call plugin tools directly — they must use workarounds like `gh api` or `curl`.

### Current behavior

- Plugin registers tools (e.g. `github_get_repo_structure`, `github_read_file_content`)
- Tools appear in Paperclip's tool registry (`/api/plugins/tools`)
- Tools are available via `POST /api/plugins/tools/execute`
- **But** Cursor/Claude Code agents do NOT see these tools in their tool list
- Managed skills can document the tools, but agents cannot invoke them natively

### Expected behavior

Plugin tools should be bridged as MCP tools (or equivalent) to the agent's adapter runtime, so agents can call them like any other tool:

```
Use tool: github_get_repo_structure
Parameters: { "repo_full_name": "owner/repo" }
```

### Proposed approach

When an agent has plugin tools available (via company skill library or direct assignment):

1. The adapter (Cursor/Claude Code) queries the plugin tool registry at agent startup
2. Each plugin tool is exposed as an MCP tool with the plugin's `parametersSchema`
3. When the agent invokes the tool, the adapter proxies the call to `POST /api/plugins/tools/execute`
4. Results are returned to the agent as tool output

### Why this matters

- Plugin tools are the primary way to extend agent capabilities (GitHub access, Jira, Slack, etc.)
- Without MCP bridging, plugins are limited to UI-only interactions or skill-documented workarounds
- The `agent.tools.register` capability suggests tools should be agent-accessible, but they're not in practice
- This blocks the full plugin ecosystem potential

### Context

We built the `@gaud_erp/paperclip-github-manager` plugin with 9 tools and a managed skill. The agent (CEO, Cursor adapter) found the skill and followed the workflow, but had to use `gh api` as transport instead of calling tools nati

title: Claude Code Review Report
text:
Recently, I ran Claude Code across several projects to look for potential issues.

In previous runs, a significant portion of reported findings turned out to be incorrect or minor false positives, but a non-trivial subset was valid and included real issues ranging from incorrect comments to actual logic bugs. As a result, the findings generally require manual validation to separate noise from actionable problems.

In this particular run, the tool appeared to over-focus on potential panic paths, which may have caused other types of issues to be underexplored or missed.

Example findings:

### C-27. JPEG2000: typo uses `lab.ra` where `lab.rb` is intended

**File:** `hayro-jpeg2000/src/lib.rs:642`
**Category:** Bug (silent wrong output)

```rust
let rb = lab.ra.unwrap_or(200);
```

This produces wrong CIE Lab → RGB output for any JPEG2000 image with
explicit Lab parameters. The `CieLab` struct in `colr.rs:88` correctly
defines both `ra` and `rb`.

**Fix:** `lab.rb.unwrap_or(200)`.

### H-17. AES PKCS#7 padding has dead conditional

**File:** `hayro-syntax/src/crypto/aes.rs:383-389`
**Category:** Maintainability (latent bug)

```rust
let pad_len = 16 - (data.len() % 16);
if pad_len == 0 {                                   // unreachable
    padded_data.extend(vec![16_u8; 16]);
} else {
    padded_data.extend(vec![pad_len as u8; pad_len]);
}
```

`pad_len` is always in `1..=16`; the `== 0` arm is dead. The else arm
happens to produce the correct PKCS#7 output, but the dead branch
invites someone to “fix” the padding and break it.

**Fix:** Drop the `if`.





Full report - [findings.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27858632/findings.md)

Newer report(full of false positives and edge cases so needs to be carefully verified)

[findings-interactive.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28504791/findings-interactive.html)

title: feat(mcp): bridge plugin-registered tools to Claude Code / Cursor / Kimi adapters
text:
Tracks upstream [paperclipai/paperclip#6707](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/issues/6707).

## Problem

Today plugin tools registered via `agent.tools.register` only work via REST. They are invisible to the Claude Code, Cursor, and Kimi adapters' native tool lists. Agents must `curl` plugin endpoints by hand — slow, error-prone, and impossible to discover.

## Why this matters for Levi

This is the **single biggest unlock for the agent-skill ecosystem.** Levi's diverged tree already has document-annotation tooling, codex integration, OPEA-specific skills. Right now an agent that wants to call any of these has to shell out to curl with hand-rolled JSON. Bridging plugin tools as native MCP tools makes the entire plugin surface first-class for the adapters Levi actually uses — agents become genuinely capable rather than just "shell scripts in trench coats."

Without this, "skill expansion" stays cosmetic.

## Required components

- Generic `@paperclipai/mcp-bridge` package that converts plugin tool manifests into MCP tool schemas
- Per-adapter wiring (Claude Code, Cursor, Kimi-local) to register the bridge as an MCP server at runtime
- Schema validation: plugin tool params translated to MCP `inputSchema` JSON Schema

## Effort

**L** — net-new design work; upstream hasn't shipped a PR yet. But the surface is well-scoped: one bridge package, ~3 adapter integrations.

## Risk

**M** — MCP tool schemas have to match plugin manifest shapes. Test coverage non-trivial.

## Levi-specific implementation note

Implement as a generic `packages/mcp-bridge` package the adapters consume — keeps the surface portable upstream if/when paperclip ships their own. Start by bridging Levi's existing document-annotation plugin as the proof of concept, then add the rest.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A plugin tool declared via `agent.tools.register` appears in the Claude Code MCP tool list at runtime
- [ ] Same for Cursor and Kimi adapters
- [ ] Param schemas round-trip: plugin man

text:
# Unblock plugin installs in Claude / Codex / Gemini / Copilot / Cursor / VS Code

## Problem

The plugin scaffolding in this repo (`.claude-plugin/`, `.codex-plugin/`, `.cursor-plugin/`, `gemini-extension.json`, `mcp.json`) all reference an npm package that doesn't exist:

```json
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "documentdb-mcp-server"]
```

```
$ npm view documentdb-mcp-server
npm error 404  Unpublished on 2025-04-17T14:13:45.796Z
```

So **the plugin installs are broken in every client today**. v2 will publish to npm under a scoped name; this issue tracks the **interim fix** so customers can use the plugins now.

## Approach

Switch every plugin config from the dead npm name to the public-GitHub spec that `npx` understands natively:

```json
"args": ["-y", "github:microsoft/documentdb-mcp#v1.0.0"]
```

This requires `microsoft/documentdb-mcp` to be public first — tracked in [microsoft/documentdb-mcp#TBD](https://github.com/microsoft/documentdb-mcp/issues).

## Tasks (in order)

- [ ] Wait for `microsoft/documentdb-mcp` to be made public and tagged `v1.0.0`
- [ ] Open PR swapping the MCP command in **all** of these files in lockstep:
  - [ ] `mcp.json`
  - [ ] `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (if it duplicates the command — currently inherits from `mcp.json`)

title: Graphify vs Claude Code AI agent
text:
Hi Team,

I have been using Graphify within my organization and encouraging others to adopt it as well. However, one challenge I am observing is that, for many common queries, Claude Code alone seems to provide similar results with the same or even lower token consumption compared to using Graphify.

Because of this, it has been difficult to convince others about the additional value Graphify brings. The common feedback I hear is:
“Claude Code already works well enough — why do we need Graphify on top of it?”

Another observation is around token usage. When Claude Code invokes the Graphify Query CLI multiple times (for example, 3–4 invocations), each query can consume around ~2K tokens. This quickly adds up to 8K+ tokens for a single workflow. In comparison, similar queries using Claude Code with grep/find/ripgrep often complete with much lower token usage.

For context, my current corpus size is:

## Corpus Check
- Large corpus: 1484 files · ~789,872 words. 

## Summary
- 10202 nodes · 17610 edges · 560 communities 

I would really appreciate guidance on the ideal use cases where Graphify clearly differentiates itself from standard Claude Code workflows.

title: Product idea: Postrule as an installable AI-coding-agent skill (Claude Code / Cursor / Windsurf / Aider)
text:
## Feature

Ship Postrule as an installable skill / extension for AI coding agents.

\`\`\`bash
npx skills add postrule           # generic surface
# or platform-specific:
claude skills install postrule    # Claude Code
cursor skill add postrule         # Cursor
# … etc
\`\`\`

Outcome: developers using AI coding agents get idiomatic Postrule behavior without having to read docs.

## What the skill bundles

- **\`@ml_switch\` semantics** — what it is, when to use it, when *not* to
- **Idiomatic instrumentation patterns** — when to drop in vs. wrap vs. AST-init
- **Classifier stdlib awareness** (#97) — agent reaches for \`from postrule.classifiers import isTypo\` before writing a fresh switch from scratch
- **Phase model + McNemar-gate rules** — agent doesn't suggest premature graduations or skip statistical gates
- **SDK / CLI reference** — login, init, analyze, bench, doctor verbs in canonical form
- **Anti-patterns** — explicit rules for what *not* to do (e.g., don't decorate functions called <100×/day, don't wrap pure-numeric logic, etc.)

## Behavioral, not just informational

The skill should tell the agent **when *not* to suggest a switch**, not just how to add one. Examples:

- Don't decorate functions called <100×/day (not enough data to graduate meaningfully)
- Don't decorate pure-numeric logic (no LLM-cost lever)
- Don't suggest \`ML_PRIMARY\` graduation without a passing McNemar gate
- Prefer \`from postrule.classifiers\` over a fresh switch when an equivalent stdlib function exists

Without this discipline the skill becomes a recipe-spammer and reduces user trust in agent-suggested Postrule usage.

## Phasing sketch

- **v0**: Claude Code skill — single skill file with the bundled content above, distributed via the \`postrule\` PyPI package's data files + a \`postrule skills install\` CLI verb
- **v1**: Cursor + Windsurf adapters (same content, platform-specific manifest format)
- **v2**: Aider + Continue + generic VSCode extension
- **v3**: Skill auto-u
